carbohydrate_map.note: These literature records describe tomato fruit or fruit cell walls, but not the specific USDA grape-tomato sample. No compatible amounts are shown. Cultivar, ripeness, and tissue can change the sugar profile. A building block shown below is a chemically bound residue within a polymer unless explicitly labeled as a free sugar.

sources.name: Systematic analysis of the sugar accumulation mechanism in sucrose- and hexose-accumulating cherry tomato fruits
sources.citation: Sun et al. (2022), BMC Plant Biology 22:303. Two Solanum lycopersicum var. cerasiforme lines; sugars analyzed across fruit stages and whole fruit, exocarp, mesocarp, endocarp, placenta, and septum.

sources.name: Remodeling of pectin and hemicelluloses in tomato pericarp during fruit growth
sources.citation: Guillon et al. (2017), Plant Science 257:48–62. Cell-wall composition and polysaccharide structure in Solanum lycopersicum var. Levovil pericarp across developmental stages.
sources.license: Citation and linked abstract; publisher terms apply to full text.

sources.name: The Structure and Composition of Extracted Pectin and Residual Cell Wall Material from Processing Tomato
sources.citation: Van Audenhove et al. (2021), Foods 10(5):1064. Pectin and residual cell-wall material from processing tomato; structural context and extraction-based characterization.

records.name: Glucose
records.part: Tomato fruit: whole fruit and fruit tissues were analyzed in the cited cherry-tomato study.
records.relationship: Measured as a soluble sugar in two cherry-tomato lines. It is also a structural repeat unit in cellulose and the backbone of xyloglucan; those bound residues are not free glucose.
records.sample_context: Two experimental cherry-tomato lines, TB0023 and TB0278, sampled at multiple ripening stages; not the USDA grape-tomato sample.

records.name: Fructose
records.part: Tomato fruit: whole fruit and fruit tissues were analyzed in the cited cherry-tomato study.
records.relationship: Measured as a soluble sugar in two cherry-tomato lines. Its abundance differed with the line and developmental stage.
records.sample_context: Two experimental cherry-tomato lines, TB0023 and TB0278, sampled at multiple ripening stages; not the USDA grape-tomato sample.

records.name: Sucrose
records.part: Tomato fruit: whole fruit and fruit tissues were analyzed in the cited cherry-tomato study.
records.relationship: A disaccharide made of one glucose unit and one fructose unit. The study found a strong cultivar difference: sucrose accumulated in TB0023 and was very low in the hexose-accumulating TB0278 line.
records.sample_context: Two experimental cherry-tomato lines, TB0023 and TB0278, sampled at multiple ripening stages; not the USDA grape-tomato sample.

records.name: Pectin
records.part: Fruit cell wall, including tomato pericarp; cell-wall structures were studied in processing tomato and Levovil pericarp.
records.relationship: Pectin is a family of polymers, not one molecule. Homogalacturonan (HG) has α-(1→4)-linked galacturonic-acid residues. Rhamnogalacturonan I (RG-I) has a rhamnose–galacturonic-acid backbone with galactose- and arabinose-rich side chains.

building_blocks.name: Galacturonic acid (GalA)
building_blocks.role: α-(1→4)-linked repeat in homogalacturonan; also part of the RG-I backbone

building_blocks.name: Rhamnose (Rha)
building_blocks.role: alternates with GalA in the RG-I backbone

building_blocks.name: Galactose
building_blocks.role: common residue in RG-I side chains; not asserted here as free galactose

building_blocks.name: Arabinose
building_blocks.role: common residue in RG-I side chains; not asserted here as free arabinose

records.sample_context: Tomato cell-wall studies used processing-tomato material and the Levovil cultivar at specified fruit-development stages; they do not quantify pectin in this USDA sample.

records.name: Cellulose
records.part: Tomato fruit cell wall; characterized in processing-tomato cell-wall material.
records.relationship: Long, linear glucan chains joined by β-(1→4) bonds. A glucose unit in cellulose is a bound residue, not free glucose.

building_blocks.name: β-D-glucose
building_blocks.role: repeating residue joined by β-(1→4) bonds

records.sample_context: Cellulose was estimated in extraction fractions from processing-tomato cell walls; no amount is available for this USDA grape-tomato sample.

records.name: Xyloglucan
records.relationship: A β-(1→4)-glucose backbone with xylose residues attached. Tomato pericarp studies report xyloglucan remodeling during fruit development.

building_blocks.name: β-D-glucose
building_blocks.role: repeating backbone residue joined by β-(1→4) bonds

building_blocks.name: Xylose
building_blocks.role: side-chain residue attached to the backbone

records.sample_context: Pericarp evidence comes from the Levovil tomato at defined developmental stages; structural detail is paired with a processing-tomato cell-wall study.

part_context.note: These are research leads for tomato parts, not accepted measurements for the USDA grape-tomato sample. Expand a source before contributing a tissue-specific claim.

parts.label: Flesh
parts.summary: Tomato fruit studies have analyzed soluble sugars in the mesocarp and endocarp, and developmental metabolomics studies have profiled mesocarp separately. Pericarp cell-wall work provides context for pectin and hemicellulose.
parts.sample_context: The sugar study used two cherry-tomato lines at multiple ripening stages. Other studies used named research cultivars and developmental samples, not this USDA grape-tomato lot.

sources.name: Systematic analysis of the sugar accumulation mechanism in sucrose- and hexose-accumulating cherry tomato fruits
sources.citation: Sun et al. (2022), BMC Plant Biology 22:303; sugar levels measured in whole fruit and multiple tissues, including mesocarp and endocarp.

sources.name: NMR-Based Tissular and Developmental Metabolomics of Tomato Fruit
sources.citation: Tomato tissues including exocarp, mesocarp, columella/placenta, locular tissue, and seeds analyzed at four developmental stages.

sources.name: Remodeling of pectin and hemicelluloses in tomato pericarp during fruit growth
sources.citation: Guillon et al. (2017), Plant Science 257:48–62; cell-wall structure studied in Levovil pericarp during fruit development.
sources.license: Citation and linked abstract; publisher terms apply to full text.

parts.label: Skin
parts.summary: Studies have compared tomato peel/exocarp with flesh and measured soluble sugars by fruit tissue. Metabolomics features need compound-level identification review before they become accepted names in this profile.
parts.sample_context: The sources use multiple tomato cultivars or experimental lines; peel results are not whole-fruit amounts and do not identify the cultivar in the USDA grape-tomato sample.

sources.name: Systematic analysis of the sugar accumulation mechanism in sucrose- and hexose-accumulating cherry tomato fruits
sources.citation: Sun et al. (2022), BMC Plant Biology 22:303; sugar levels measured in exocarp and other fruit tissues.

sources.name: A Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolome Database for Tomato
sources.citation: Moco et al. (2006); LC-QTOF/PDA tomato fruit database and peel/flesh comparison across a pool of 96 cultivars and several fruit types.

sources.name: NMR-Based Tissular and Developmental Metabolomics of Tomato Fruit
sources.citation: Developmental profiles include separately dissected exocarp and other tomato fruit tissues.

parts.label: Seeds
parts.summary: Tomato studies have profiled seeds separately from flesh. Dry, developing, and imbibed seed samples are distinct states; their results should not be treated as measurements of fresh seeds inside this raw grape tomato.
parts.sample_context: Available studies use developmental-stage samples or mapping populations and require state, genotype, and tissue checks before any claim is transferred.

sources.name: NMR-Based Tissular and Developmental Metabolomics of Tomato Fruit
sources.citation: Tomato seeds separated from fruit tissues and profiled at four developmental stages.

sources.name: Metabolomic analysis of tomato seed germination
sources.citation: GC-TOF/MS profiles of dry mature and 6-hour imbibed seeds from a Moneymaker × S. pimpinellifolium mapping population.
